ambiguousKey.note: An ambiguous key, constructed: one sub-district given a second, different company
ambiguousKey.constructed: No sub-district in Table XII carries two companies. The row is added here because the case cannot be drawn from the data.
ambiguousKey.fieldworkRefused: The second table gives "St. Saviour, Southwark" more than one "water_supply": "Southwark and Vauxhall Company only" and "Lambeth Company only". Relating cannot choose between them, and choosing would put a value on these rows that the table does not support. Check whether "sub_district" identifies one row of the second table.
ambiguousKey.whatTheRefusalBuys: A merge returns 66 rows where the left table has 64, because the 2 rows for that key each match twice. Both companies would then appear in the stratification, each carrying the same population, and no total in the result reveals it.

notEstablished: That exact matching is the right matching. Snow's two tables spell every sub-district identically, so this data never exercises a name that differs by punctuation or case -- the case a practitioner will actually meet. Fieldwork folds surrounding whitespace and nothing else, by decision rather than by this result.
That relating is right for bringing MEASURES across. That adds rows rather than a column and is deliberately not built, so nothing here speaks to it.

That the category is the right stratifier. Snow's third group -- sub-districts supplied by both companies -- is 300,149 of the 486,936 people in the table, and what to do with it is the practitioner's judgement, not an outcome of the join.
